rationale: Audited every fact's cited operands against its receipt and found one more transposition of the same kind as the last correction: the client-change fact said the leader had reconstructed one voter against the three voters recorded at index 110 in its own log, but its receipt records that configuration entry at log index 106 — 110 is the entry of the five-voter discard case. The statement now cites 106, the premise note explains the source of the error, and every other fact's cited operands matched its receipt in this audit.

knowledge.statement: In the retained client-change execution the committed membership was rewritten without the replaced configuration's majority: the leader had reconstructed one voter against the three voters recorded at log index 106 in its own log, its client AddVoter with prevIndex 0 completed (change_committed true), and its configuration afterwards had two voters — itself and the fresh instance, which was not part of the replaced configuration — with the two peers that had held votes there carried as nonvoters. Both of those peers, restarted with the flag disabled, adopted the rewritten configuration (demoted_peers_adopted 2) and held no vote in it (demoted_peers_with_vote 0), while with the flag disabled the same node could not be leader with the others down, the change failed with "node is not the leader" and both peers kept their votes.
knowledge.conditions: Three-voter committed configuration recorded at log index 106 while the restarted leader's snapshot metadata carries a single-voter configuration; only the leader and one fresh empty instance run while the change is issued, and the fresh instance is connected to the leader in both directions; the two peers of the committed configuration are restarted afterwards with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled. The change is the package's own AddVoter with prevIndex 0; no partition, no concurrent client change and no nonzero prevIndex case is exercised.
knowledge.changed_premise: The earlier revision cited log index 110 for the configuration entry in the leader's own log. That index belongs to the five-voter discard case; the client-change receipt records its entry at log index 106, and an audit of every fact against its receipts found the other operands unchanged. The consequence and its conditions are unaffected.
